metadata.note: The Adirondack Branch -- Saratoga Springs to North Creek, and after 1944 on to Tahawus. Dr. Thomas Clark Durant, vice-president of the Union Pacific, built the Adirondack Company's line up the Hudson from Saratoga between the mid-1860s and 1871 to open his Adirondack land holdings to tourists; from North Creek passengers went on by stage to Blue Mountain Lake and by water to Raquette Lake. The Delaware and Hudson bought it July 11 1889 and merged it Nov 5 1902, running it as the Adirondack Branch. Its two most famous days bracket the branch's character: Sep 14 1901, when Theodore Roosevelt came down off Mount Marcy to North Creek station and left it as president, and the 1930s ski trains from Schenectady and New York City that carried Gore Mountain traffic through the Depression. Passenger service went summer-only in 1950 and ended in 1957. During the war the federal Defense Plant Corporation blasted a 29-mile extension up the Hudson headwaters from North Creek to the National Lead ilmenite workings at Tahawus, finished in 1944 and worked for ore until the mine closed in September 1989. Passengers returned as excursions: the Upper Hudson River Railroad, North Creek to Riparius, 1999-2010; the Saratoga and North Creek Railway over the full 57 miles, Jul 14 2011 to Apr 7 2018; and the Saratoga, Corinth and Hudson from 2022 over the southern end, Corinth 7.1 miles south to Greenfield, with spring festival trains north over the Sacandaga River to Hadley from 2023. Neither reaches Saratoga Springs. See dh_lake_george_branch.geojson and scranton_railroads.geojson for other D&H lines.

metadata.not_yet_sourced: Headways are estimates in every era; no D&H timetable has been consulted, and the two excursion operators' schedules are described qualitatively rather than as headways. The staged opening of the original line is not represented: sources give only 'built from the mid-1860s, reached North Creek 1871', so the whole 57 miles appears at once in 1871 even though the railhead moved north over several years -- the intermediate opening dates have not been found. No passenger service is documented on either the Tahawus extension or the Warrensburg branch; both are drawn because they are part of the D&H network, with placeholder headways that should not be read as service. The Saratoga, Corinth and Hudson excursion extents were re-checked against the operator's site on 2026-08-26 and are now drawn Corinth-Greenfield and Corinth-Hadley; what remains unsourced there is the frequency, which varies by season and event. Wikipedia's 62-mile figure for Saratoga-North Creek conflicts with the 57 miles quoted for the same track by the Saratoga and North Creek Railway and with the 56.69-mile digitized trace; the shorter figure is used. The 1957 end date is the documented end of passenger service, not a dated last train.

segments.note: Built by Dr. Thomas Clark Durant, vice-president of the Union Pacific, from 1864-1866 to 1871, reaching North Creek in 1871; the North Creek depot went up in 1872 and still stands. The railroad existed to carry tourists to Durant's Adirondack properties -- passengers went on from North Creek by stage 28 miles to Blue Mountain Lake and then by water to Raquette Lake. Control passed to Durant's son William West Durant after his death. Frequency estimated/unsourced

properties.line: Saratoga, Corinth and Hudson: Corinth – Greenfield
properties.speed_source: estimated: tourist excursion speed; the advertised 1.5-hour round trip over 7.1 miles each way implies well under 25 km/h including the layover, so this is an upper bound and is unsourced

segments.note: The Saratoga, Corinth and Hudson began excursions over the southern end of the old Adirondack Branch in 2022, running out of Corinth Station at 9 Railroad Place. The standard trip is a 1.5-hour round trip 7.1 miles south to Greenfield and back; shorter rides turn at Kings Station or LaMothe Landing. Themed trains run through the year -- Maple in April, Cottontail Express, Sunset Limited, Autumn Explorer, Pumpkin Picker, Candy Cane Express, Moonlight Moonshine Express -- and the railroad was still advertising them for 2026. No train runs through to Saratoga Springs: the roughly 9 miles from Greenfield south to the Amtrak station carry no passengers and are not drawn. Frequency varies by season and event; the daily headway here is a placeholder.
sources: Segment-level: the operator's own site gives the Corinth departure point, the Greenfield turnaround and the "about seven miles" run; Railfan & Railroad dates the start of Corinth-Greenfield rides to 2022.

properties.line: Saratoga, Corinth and Hudson: Corinth – Hadley

segments.note: Excursions north from Corinth across the Sacandaga River to Hadley returned Apr 29 2023, the first passenger train over that bridge since the Saratoga and North Creek quit in 2018, run in partnership with the Hadley-Luzerne Maple Festival. The Maple in April Hadley Express has continued as a seasonal offering, boarding at either Corinth or Hadley. This leg runs only for those spring festival trains, not on the year-round Corinth-Greenfield schedule, so the daily headway is a placeholder and the drawn years cover only the seasons in which the trip was offered.
